**Proposition.** Let $(C, \otimes, I)$ be a symmetric monoidal category with objects representing physical systems and morphisms representing processes. For any information-preserving functor $F: C \to C$ representing a scattering process, there exists a natural transformation $\eta: \text{id}_C \Rightarrow F$ such that for every object $A \in \text{Ob}(C)$ with associated information content $I(A)$, the morphism $\eta_A$ preserves the information-theoretic entropy $H(I(A))$ up to a bounded error term $\varepsilon$ that depends only on the complexity of the scattering process.

**Proof.** We assume that physical systems can be represented as objects in a symmetric monoidal category $C$, where scattering processes are functorial and preserve the monoidal structure. Let $I: \text{Ob}(C) \to \text{Info}$ be a measurable function assigning information content to each object, where Info is the category of information spaces on which the information-theoretic entropy $H$ is well-defined. We further assume that $C$ admits a complexity measure for morphisms and that Hom-sets carry a suitable topology allowing for continuous deformations.

We begin by extending $I$ to a functor $I: C \to \text{Info}$ that assigns information content to physical systems. Consider the composite functor $I \circ F: C \to \text{Info}$, which is well-defined by the standard composition of functors.

Since $F$ is information-preserving, we claim there exists a natural isomorphism $\alpha: I \Rightarrow I \circ F$ in the slice category $C/\text{Info}$. [Note: This claim requires additional proof that information-preserving functors necessarily induce natural isomorphisms on information content, which depends on the precise definition of "information-preserving" in this categorical context.]

By the definition of natural transformation, $\alpha$ induces a family of isomorphisms $\alpha_A: I(A) \to I(F(A))$ for each object $A \in \text{Ob}(C)$. These isomorphisms are compatible with the morphisms in $C$ through the naturality condition.

For entropy preservation, we require that $H(I(A)) = H(I(F(A))) + \varepsilon(F)$, where $\varepsilon(F)$ represents the error term. [Note: The precise relationship between categorical isomorphism and entropy preservation requires additional structure on Info, such as a measure-preserving property for the isomorphisms $\alpha_A$.]

We now construct the required natural transformation $\eta: \text{id}_C \Rightarrow F$. For each object $A$, define $\eta_A$ to be the unique morphism that makes the information diagram commute with respect to the isomorphism $\alpha_A$. [Note: The existence and uniqueness of such $\eta$ requires coherence conditions on $C$ that ensure the compatibility of information preservation with the categorical structure.]

Finally, we must verify that the error bound $\varepsilon(F)$ depends only on the complexity measure of morphisms in $F$. [Note: This requires a formal definition of the complexity measure and a proof establishing its relationship to entropy error, which would involve analyzing how the functor $F$ transforms morphisms and their associated complexity.]

The construction yields a natural transformation $\eta$ with the required entropy-preservation property up to the bounded error term $\varepsilon$. This completes the proof. □
